correctness.rationale: For a nonempty finite set in a meet-tree, fix one element s. All meets s∧x lie on the same lower chain; their minimum is the meet of the full set. Therefore every finitely generated point is a pairwise meet (allowing x=s), a fact that uses semilinearity and not just associativity. In the finite closure, unselected vertices must have two child branches containing selected points. Conversely each such vertex is the meet of marked leaves in two of its branches. The age property realizes every permitted shape, and meet-language ultrahomogeneity identifies exactly the isomorphic colored closures. The ordinary multiset cycle index applies to the unordered children; each term is rooted at a marked point or at an unmarked point with two or more children, and root weights determine a unique solution by total degree. If a vertex has k+1 children at n=k+1, each branch consumes its only marked point as a leaf, and neither the vertex nor an ancestor can be marked or carry any additional branch with a leaf. Thus the only excluded type is the unmarked star. The excess-child count over internal vertices is L-1 for L leaves, so w≤L−1≤n−1, equality forces full binary branching with only leaves marked, and binary trees with an extra unary marked chain realize the full range. The chain case k=1 gives z/(1-z). originality.rationale: The unrestricted colored shape model and its grading are already implicit in the earlier ordered-tuple orbit result: quotienting injective tuple orbits by coordinate permutations forgets precisely the marked labels and preserves overhead. No standalone originality is credited to that implication, the OEIS totals, the classical multiset equation, or the Fraïssé construction. The finding's distinct arity-sensitive assertion is the sharp first-difference law with its exact one-orbit witness, together with the overhead endpoint characterization uniform across all caps k≥2. No inspected source states these threshold and rank results for finite subset orbits.
residual_risks: The unrestricted model is specifically covered by a prior equivalent quotient, regardless of indexing terminology. Distinct unindexed work on the all-vertex cap or relative arity ranks may exist; this is a bounded comparison, not a priority certification.

value.rationale: The arity bound is a structural parameter of the homogeneous limit; a precise smallest rank of unordered subset data that recovers it is useful in comparing those limits through their orbit profiles. The first extra orbit has an explicit geometric witness and exact overhead, and the other endpoint identifies a rank whose counts cannot detect any arity ≥2. This is a quantified result for every k and n, not value ascribed to computing another entry of the classical Greg-tree table.
